summary: This note is a Wikipedia article on Sky UK, covering the launch of BSkyB's fee-based satellite service in 1993, its closure of the analogue service in 2001, and later developments. It also covers a 2013 trademark dispute with Microsoft over SkyDrive, the platform reaching 10 million homes in 2010, Sky+ pricing and features, and a 2012 controversy over benefits claimants' Sky subscriptions.
one_line: Overview of Sky UK's history as BSkyB, from its 1993 fee-based satellite launch to its later subscriber, Sky+ and trademark milestones.
key_facts: The Sky service started on 1 September 1993, based on an idea from chief executive Sam Chisholm and Rupert Murdoch to make the business entirely fee-based.
The new 1993 package included four channels formerly available free-to-air, broadcast on Astra's satellites, plus new channels.
The analogue service closed on 27 September 2001 due to the launch and expansion of the Sky Digital platform.
Within two months of the 1993 launch, BSkyB gained 400,000 new subscribers, helping it reach 3.5 million households by mid-1994.
Michael Grade criticized the operations before the Select Committee on National Heritage, mainly for the lack of original programming on many new channels.
In July 2013, the English High Court of Justice found that Microsoft's use of the term "SkyDrive" infringed Sky's right to the "Sky" trademark.
On 31 July 2013, BSkyB and Microsoft announced a settlement in which Microsoft would not appeal and would rename its SkyDrive service.
On 27 January 2014, Microsoft announced that SkyDrive will soon become OneDrive, and SkyDrive Pro becomes OneDrive for Business.
BSkyB's direct-to-home satellite service became available in 10 million homes in 2010, Europe's first pay-TV platform to achieve that milestone.
The 10 million home target reached 36% of UK households, an audience of more than 25m people.
The target was first announced in August 2004, and an additional 2.4m customers subscribed to the service since then.
From 1 July 2007, customers subscribing to any BSkyB package get Sky+ included at no extra charge.
In January 2010 BSkyB discontinued the Sky+ Box and started issuing the Sky+HD Box as standard.
As of 31 March 2008, Sky had 3,393,000 Sky+ users.
In 2012 the Daily Mail reported that the benefits agency was checking claimants' Sky TV bills to see if single mothers were wrongly claiming to live alone.
